title: Pagination
learning_outcomes: Explain the purpose of pagination and when it is appropriate.
Apply pagination structure using the documented Bootstrap 5.3 pattern.
Check previous and next controls and identify one likely failure mode.

content.intro: In this lesson, you will study pagination and connect it to a small implementation or review task. The included subtopics preserve the attached Bootstrap curriculum outline.
content.why_it_matters: Pagination gives an interface a recognizable pattern, but it does not replace good semantic HTML. Choose the component that matches the meaning of the content and test its action, focus, and responsive behavior.

content.task: Compose a realistic example with pagination. Make its purpose clear in the HTML and check that interactive controls use the correct semantic element.
task_acceptance_criteria: Explain the purpose and appropriate use of pagination.
Use the documented class, component, API, or workflow correctly.
Record a responsive, accessibility, or build verification relevant to this example.

common_mistakes.problem: Treating pagination as a visual-only change.
common_mistakes.why: A class or style does not automatically add semantic meaning, application logic, or secure server behavior.
common_mistakes.fix: Use the appropriate HTML semantics and verify the actual interaction.

common_mistakes.problem: Checking only the default viewport or happy path.
common_mistakes.why: Responsive changes and interaction states can reveal issues that are not visible in a single screenshot.
common_mistakes.fix: Repeat the task at a narrow and a wide viewport and include keyboard/error state checks where relevant.
